title: Beyond a Single Sentiment Score: Topical and Affective Dimensions of Emoji Meaning on Twitter
Beyond a Single Sentiment Score: Topical and Affective Dimensions of Emoji Meaning on Twitter
summary: The paper argues that representing an emoji by a single sentiment scalar collapses two dissociable dimensions of meaning: how topically coherent its contexts are and how affectively dispersed its crowd-sourced ratings are. It introduces 'stability delta', the within-class minus between-class mean cosine similarity of all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings of emoji-free tweet text, computes it for the 62 emojis with at least 15 occurrences in the Emoji Sarcasm Dataset, and correlates it with external per-emoji affect-dispersion measures. The headline result is a positive Spearman correlation with Kralj Novak sentiment variance (rho = +0.361, Holm p = 0.015, n = 59) corroborated by Ferre 2025 strongly-evoked-emotion counts (rho = +0.509, p = 0.0003, n = 47), with a saturated (>0.97 macro F1) sarcasm classifier reported only as supporting evidence.

why: The inspected repository is the original Emoji Sarcasm Dataset release (jsubram/Sarcasm-Detection-Using-Emoji), not the analysis code for this paper. It supplies the Twitter CSV needed for C1 but contains no implementation of stability delta, emosent matching, permutation/BCa inference, or the four-test Holm family. The paper's own code link (anonymous.4open.science/r/StableContextsMixedFeelings) was not cloned/available in the inspection, so the C1 pipeline must be reimplemented from the paper's equations and the claim contract.
est_runtime: About 8-12 minutes: install/download packages and MiniLM (~4 min), embed about 16k short tweets on CPU (~2-4 min), compute deltas and 10k permutations/BCa on 59 points (<1 min).
blockers: Inspected repo is a dataset release, not the paper's analysis code
No GPU on this machine; C1 is CPU-only anyway
emosent-py is not installed and must be checked on Python 3.12
Exact background-tweet sampling seed and cleaning details are not specified, so rho may differ slightly

approach: Reimplement only the C1 pipeline, because the inspected repository is the Emoji Sarcasm Dataset release, not the paper's analysis code. Clone and load the ESD Twitter partition, apply the 85% ASCII English filter, canonicalize emojis, take the first emoji as primary, build the >=15-occurrence 62-emoji panel, and encode emoji-free lowercased text with all-MiniLM-L6-v2. For each panel emoji, sample up to 100 within-emoji tweets and 500 background tweets, compute delta = W_e - B_e, join to emosent-py, and run the 59-emoji Spearman with 10,000 permutations, percentile and BCa bootstrap CIs, Holm correction over the four Kralj Novak tests, and partial Spearman controlling for emoji frequency. The final `python reproduce.py` writes `results/metrics.json`; C3 descriptive delta checks are logged as sanity evidence, while C4-C6 classifier claims and their R11-R13 requirements are out of scope for this CPU C1 reproduction.
steps: Create working directories and install CPU dependencies with pip: sentence-transformers, emoji, emosent-py, and nltk if supplementary checks are enabled; verify imports of numpy, scipy, pandas, sentence_transformers, emoji, and emosent.

If data is absent, git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/jsubram/Sarcasm-Detection-Using-Emoji into data/raw/esd; confirm Data/Final_Dataset_Twitter.csv exists and load it with pandas, preserving tweet order.

Run src/prepare_data.py: apply the 85% ASCII English filter to raw text, assert the exact count 16587 (or log and diagnose if off by a few), detect all emojis with the emoji library, strip U+1F3FB-U+1F3FF and U+FE0F, take the first canonical emoji as primary_emoji, build emoji-free lowercased clean_text, drop no-emoji tweets, and assert 16575 final corpus rows.

Build the analytical panel: count primary_emoji occurrences, retain emojis with count >= 15, and assert 62 emojis covering 15569 tweets; save data/processed/tweets.parquet and results/preprocess_counts.json.

Run src/embed_text.py: load SentenceTransformer('all-MiniLM-L6-v2') on CPU, encode clean_text with batch_size=64, normalize_embeddings=True, save float32 embeddings.npy aligned to the processed tweet index.

Run src/stability_delta.py with RNG seed 42: for each panel emoji in sorted codepoint order, sample up to 100 within tweets and 500 background tweets from primary_emoji != e, compute W_e as mean off-diagonal dot product, B_e as mean cross-pair dot product, delta = W_e - B_e, and save results/deltas.csv; also compute C3 sanity statistics.

Run src/kralj_novak.py: import emosent-py, inspect available per-emoji fields if names differ, canonicalize lexicon keys, match the panel, compute variance ddof=0 over (p_neg,p_neu,p_pos), and save results/kralj_novak.csv; assert n=59 matched emojis or print the unmatched list.

Run src/stats_battery.py: merge deltas and Kralj Novak variance, compute Spearman rho and asymptotic p, 10000 two-sided permutation p-values, 10000 percentile and BCa paired bootstrap CIs, leave-one-out jackknife range, Holm-adjusted p across the four declared Kralj Novak tests, and partial Spearman controlling for emoji frequency.

Have reproduce.py write results/metrics.json with the primary rho, n, permutation p, Holm p, bootstrap CIs, jackknife range, partial rho, delta descriptive checks, preprocessing counts, matched-emoji count, and the exact config snapshot; print a concise summary.

Compare the primary rho against the claim tolerance of 0.02 around +0.361; if outside [0.341, 0.381], inspect first-emoji definition, background sampling, clean_text emoji stripping, emosent probability field selection, and the 59-emoji matched set before accepting the run.
smoke_test: Run `python reproduce.py --smoke`: take the first 800 English-filtered ESD tweets, set min_occurrences=3, within_sample_max=20, between_sample_size=50, permutations=200, bootstrap_resamples=200, encode with the same MiniLM model, compute deltas for the first 3 qualifying emojis, match emosent-py, run Spearman/permutation/bootstrap, and require a finite rho, n>=3, and a written results/smoke_metrics.json. This proves CSV loading, filtering, emoji extraction, embedding, delta sampling, lexicon matching, and stats flow end-to-end without touching the full 16k corpus.
intermediate_checks: Dependency check: sentence-transformers, emoji, emosent-py, scipy, pandas, numpy import successfully; if emosent-py import name differs, inspect the installed package and record the callable/fields.

Dataset size check: raw DataFrame has 16859 Twitter rows; after the 85% ASCII English filter it has 16587 rows; after emoji normalization and primary-emoji extraction it has 16575 rows; after >=15-occurrence filtering it has 62 emojis covering 15569 tweets.
Label/order check if labels are loaded later: label CSV row count matches the Twitter CSV row count and no rows are silently reordered; this is not required for C1 but guards supplementary metrics.
Emoji normalization check: no panel emoji contains U+1F3FB-U+1F3FF or U+FE0F; each row has exactly one primary_emoji; emoji-only tweets are retained with an empty clean_text if present (A6).
Embedding check: embeddings.npy shape is (16575, 384), dtype float32, and row-wise L2 norms are approximately 1.0; no NaNs.

Delta sanity check: mean delta across the 62 emojis is near 0.0766, max near +0.237, min near -0.003, and 61 of 62 deltas are positive; large deviations indicate wrong primary-emoji choice, cleaning, or background sampling.
Lexicon match check: Kralj Novak matching returns exactly 59 emojis; variance values are finite, non-negative, and computed from probability triples rather than the scalar sentiment score.

Primary correlation check: Spearman rho over 59 emojis is near +0.361, permutation p is near 0.005, Holm-adjusted p is significant and near 0.015, bootstrap CI is roughly [+0.10, +0.59], and jackknife range is roughly [+0.333, +0.412].
Sanity baseline: permuting the Kralj Novak variance labels should produce rho centered near 0 with no significant p, confirming the permutation code is not leaking the pairing.
budget_plan: CPU-only budget of about 15 minutes: 4 minutes for pip installs, repo clone, and MiniLM weight download; 1 minute for the smoke test; 8-12 minutes for full preprocessing, embedding ~16.6k short tweets with all-MiniLM-L6-v2, computing 62 deltas, and running 10k permutations plus 10k percentile/BCa bootstrap resamples on 59 points. No classifier training is performed; C4-C6 are out of scope. Reserve ~3 minutes for diagnostics if the primary rho falls outside the +/-0.02 tolerance.
